name: Nabopolassar
title: Founder of the Neo-Babylonian Empire
summary: Nabopolassar was the founder of the Neo-Babylonian dynasty and father of Nebuchadnezzar II. He led the revolt against the Assyrian Empire and established Babylon as the dominant power in Mesopotamia. His military successes laid the foundation for his son's conquests, including the destruction of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Founding of the Neo-Babylonian Empire
keyEvents.description: Nabopolassar revolted against Assyria and established himself as king in Babylon in 626 BC, thus laying the foundation for the empire that would take Judah into captivity.

keyEvents.title: The Fall of Nineveh
keyEvents.description: In alliance with the Medes, Nabopolassar conquered the Assyrian capital Nineveh in 612 BC, an event prophesied by Nahum.

keyEvents.title: Babylon as a World Power
keyEvents.description: Under Nabopolassar's rule, Babylon grew to become the power that the prophets warned would punish Judah for their sin.

keyEvents.title: Nebuchadnezzar Takes Command
keyEvents.description: Nabopolassar sent his son Nebuchadnezzar to lead the army, and at the battle of Carchemish in 605 BC he defeated Egypt, shortly before Nabopolassar's death.
